gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 9 build step is the narrowest honest place to keep the runtime survey family machine-checkable without inventing a runtime loader implementation.

A dedicated survey gate keeps the mixed Phase 6 schedule wording, the real Phase 9 roadmap target, the landed shared runtime-loader seam, the new shared command_name field, and the still-absent argv or environment controls explicit on current master.
The repo already had runtime starter samples and two loader-plan files, but it still lacked one shared note that says Phase 6 should not absorb runtime allocator or init-flow work.

The bounded runtime-loader starter still needs explicit review cues for hidden runtime services, implicit allocation posture, panic behavior, and visible unsafe ownership while the shared request surface remains pre-execution.

The atomic64, bitmap, and kretprobe starter lanes now publish entry and exit symbol names, requires_runtime_substrate flags, selftest-hook markers, and handoff-stage checks that a future shared runtime loader must consume.

The shared runtime-loader blocker now sits adjacent to the freeze map's study-only `kernel/workqueue.c` anchor, so task scheduling, polling, event-loop behavior, and any workqueue-parity status change must stay blocked until the Architecture Council reopens that boundary with fresh evidence.

The roadmap's first command and environment plumbing surfaces live in Phase 8 tooling, and the shared runtime loader now carries a shared command_name field, but argv-policy and environment-derived activation handling still remain blocked.

The shared runtime-loader request surface now consumes the allocator policy contract directly, so allocator ownership, fallback rules, and init-flow posture are machine-checkable before any real runtime loader behavior exists.

The shared runtime-loader request surface now carries staged entry and exit symbol names from both sample-side loader plans, so the common lifecycle contract is explicit even though no real runtime execution path exists yet.
